Then, when the seam is rolled with bias tape, the final length of the back opening ends up being the same as the length of the seam outline. This process gives the back opening a neat, rounded shape. You'll see the visor hold its form more accurately. Next, let's apply Solidify to the crown pieces. In real hats, the front crown panels are reinforced with a stiff interlining to maintain the hat's profile. Reflecting this, apply Solidify 100 to the front crown panel. To resolve this, you can reposition it using the Superimpose under function. However, since the upper pattern's thickness now extends downward, you must assign a sufficient collision value to prevent the two patterns from overlapping. To ensure proper placement, it is recommended to set the collision thickness of the lower pattern to 3, matching the thickness of the upper pattern. If you want to add more thickness to the lower pattern, increase the value in the Additional Thickness rendering. markdown_content: ## Loading Cap Assets and Preparing Workspace This section explains how to load mid-profile cap assets, molds, and visors in Clo, emphasizing the use of consistent mold and visor types for matching silhouettes. - Open Clo library, navigate to Garment > Connect Asset tab. - Search for "mid-profile" to find male and female 6-panel cap assets with fully constructed snapbacks. - Double-click the male cap asset to load into the workspace. - Load the mid-profile Cap Mold and half-curved visor from the Avatar tab under Connect Asset. - Use the "Add" option when loading molds and visors to avoid replacing the current avatar and losing work. - Adjust the visor angle to align properly with the cap. - Select both mold and visor and set their skin offset to 0. ## Creating and Attaching Bias Tape This section covers simulating bias tape application on back openings with seam allowance considerations, aligning virtual construction closely with real production. - Back openings with seam allowances are shorter than patterns without seam allowances. - Rolling the seam with bias tape results in a final length matching the seam outline, giving a neat rounded shape. - Clo uses patterns without seam allowance by default, so simulating rolled sewing requires predicting final lengths. ### Procedure: 1. Right-click the back opening segment and select **Extend Pattern Outline**. 2. Enter seam allowance width: 0.25 inches. 3. Click the outer edge of the seam allowance to check the outline length. 4. Create a bias tape pattern: - Use Rectangle tool in 2D window. - Set width to outline length, height to 0.25 inches (seam width). 5. Right-click the bias tape center line, select **Unfold Symmetric Editing with Sewing**. 6. Remove the seam allowance pattern using the Trace tool and **Cut** on the baseline. 7. Create an internal line for sewing bias tape: - Right-click the back opening outline, select **Offset as Internal Line**. - Enter 0.25 inches (bias tape width). ## Sewing Bias Tape with Length Adjustment Considerations This section discusses how bias tape behaves during curved and straight sewing in real production, and how to replicate these effects in Clo. - Bias tape tends to follow the shorter seam line on curved edges, causing slight length shrinkage. - Straight edges like the bottom edge show minimal length change after sewing. - Areas with multiple tape layers also show little length change due to fabric thickness. - In Clo, sew bias tape at a 1:1 length ratio along straight edges and layered sections. ### Sewing Steps: 1. Use the free sewing tool to sew from the bottom edge up to where the curve begins. 2. Reference notches or the snap height to determine sewing length. 3. Right-click after starting the sewing line to input exact length. 4. Repeat sewing on the bias tape pattern, finishing at the snap point. 5. Sew curved and remaining parts with a 1:1 length ratio. 6. Change the sewing line type to **Turned**. ### Simulation Settings: - Select bias tape pattern. - Lower particle distance to 5. - Set collision thickness to 0. - Right-click tape pattern in 3D, select **Superimpose Under** to align with sewing line. - Apply **Strengthen** to entire pattern and run simulation. ## Creating a Double-Layer Quilted Sweatband This section details creating a realistic double-layer sweatband to simulate thickness and quilting effects. - Double-layer construction simulates substantial thickness like a real sweatband. - Extend top edge of sweatband: - Right-click > **Offset Pattern Outline**. - Set distance to 1 inch, check **Create Internal Line**. - Use Fold Arrangement tool on internal line to fold pattern in half. - Sew top and bottom outlines, set sewing line type to **Turned**. - Particle distance: 5, collision thickness: 0. - Run simulation. - Add quilting stitch lines: - Right-click center line > **Offset as Internal Line**. - Set number of offsets: 2, distance: 0.33 inches. - Check both sides for symmetrical quilting lines. - Sew along internal lines and run simulation. - If simulation instability occurs, adjust visor pattern position slightly forward with Gizmo to prevent collisions. ## Adding Details and Creating a Double-Layered Visor This section explains adding stitching lines, cloning visor layers, and simulating visor pad thickness for realism. - Real visors have two fabric layers wrapping a visor pad. - Add stitching lines before cloning: - Right-click visor outer edge > **Offset as Internal Line**. - Set number of offsets: 5. - Choose **Individual** distance option. - First line at 0.5 inches inward from edge. - Remaining lines spaced evenly at 0.25 inches. - Right-click visor pattern > **Layer Clone Under** to create double layer. - Clo automatically sews internal lines on cloned layer. - Select top visor pattern, apply thickness of 3 in properties to simulate visor pad. - Adjust curvature to 20% for angular edge appearance. - Increase additional thickness collision to 3 to prevent sinking of layers during simulation. - Use **Superimpose Under** on top layer for correct thickness placement. - If needed, raise bottom layer above top layer. - Select visor patterns, right-click > **Apply Solidify**. - Ensure **Freeze** is unchecked. - Set Strengthen to 80 for firmer structure. - Run simulation to hold visor shape. ## Reinforcing Crown Panels and Managing Pattern Thickness This section describes reinforcing front crown panels and managing thickness direction and collision for accurate 3D shape. - Real hats have stiff interlining in front crown panels for profile support. - Apply **Solidify 100** to front crown panels for stiffness. - Apply **Solidify 40** to remaining crown panels for softer structure. - Run simulation and check shape. - Re-sew any undone sewing lines, especially on snap patterns with seam allowances. - Visor thickness default extrusion is both directions, causing visor to rise above crown. - Change extrusion direction to **Backward** to direct thickness downward. - Lower pattern may become hidden; use **Superimpose Under** to reposition. - Assign collision thickness of 3 to lower pattern to prevent overlap. - Increase additional thickness rendering on lower pattern if needed. ## Applying Fabrics, Top Stitching, and Top Button These finishing steps are covered briefly, as they were explained in Tutorial 1: - Apply fabric textures and materials. - Add top stitching details. - Add the top button to the cap. ## Importing and Adjusting Alternative Visor Types This section covers swapping visors and adjusting settings for proper simulation. - Connect offers various visor types; this tutorial uses "Curved 1." - Double-click "Curved 1" visor asset to import. - Delete previously loaded half-curved visor. - Adjust angle and set skin offset to 0. - Delete lower pattern and remove sewing lines connecting to crown patterns. - Freeze all crown patterns. - Unfreeze and unsolidify visor pattern. - Apply Strengthen to visor. - Run simulation; visor should conform naturally. - Use negative pressure value to fit visor perfectly. - Stop simulation and apply Solidify again. - Re-sew patterns and adjust fold angle. - Reset pressure value to zero. - Un-strengthen visor pattern. - Adjust pattern and visor position to place close to crown for stability. - Run simulation again to complete curved visor setup. ## Summary This tutorial provides detailed steps to construct a realistic 6-panel mid-profile cap in Clo, covering asset loading, bias tape creation and sewing, double-layer sweatband and visor construction, crown reinforcement, fabric application, and visor swapping. The workflow emphasizes closely simulating real production processes, including seam allowances, sewing behavior on curves, layering, and structural reinforcement for accurate digital garment simulation.

visor should conform naturally. - Use negative pressure value to fit visor perfectly. - Stop simulation and apply Solidify again. - Re-sew patterns and adjust fold angle. - Reset pressure value to zero. - Un-strengthen visor pattern. - Adjust pattern and visor position to place close to crown for stability. - Run simulation again to complete curved visor setup. ## Summary This tutorial provides detailed steps to construct a realistic 6-panel mid-profile cap in Clo, covering asset loading, bias tape creation and sewing, double-layer sweatband and visor construction, crown reinforcement, fabric application, and visor swapping. The workflow emphasizes closely simulating real production processes, including seam allowances, sewing behavior on curves, layering, and structural reinforcement for accurate digital garment simulation.
